title: URL & URLSearchParams
lede: WHATWG URL parsing, query-string building, and route matching — the natural companions to fetch() for the REST-client priority. Parsing reuses libcurl's already-linked URL API rather than a hand-rolled parser. The recurring divergence is single-value-per-key: URLSearchParams is backed by a plain Map<string,string>, so a repeated key keeps only its last value and getAll() never returns more than one element. URLPattern is object-literal init only, and its exec() returns a merged Map rather than the spec's per-component result object.

entries.name: URL
entries.description: Parses an absolute URL into its component fields. Fields — href, protocol, host, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash, origin, searchParams — are plain object field reads, no dispatched methods. A part absent from the URL reads back as "", matching real URL's own default. A malformed URL throws a catchable Error ("Invalid URL"). Parsing goes through libcurl's URL API rather than a hand-rolled parser.

returns.desc: The parsed URL with its component fields.

entries.snippet:
const u = new URL("https://example.com:8080/a/b?x=1&y=hello%20world#frag")
console.log(u.hostname)  // example.com
console.log(u.port)      // 8080
console.log(u.searchParams.get("y"))  // hello world
differences: `new URL(url)` — single-argument form only, no base-URL resolution

entries.name: URLSearchParams
entries.description: Reads and builds query strings. new URLSearchParams() starts empty; new URLSearchParams(init) parses a query string and tolerates a leading '?', so passing a URL's own .search straight through just works. Backed by a plain Map<string,string>, so get/set/has/delete/size/keys()/values()/entries()/forEach() all come for free from the Map machinery, plus toString() (percent-encodes back into a query string) and getAll().

params.name: init
params.desc: Optional query string to parse (a leading '?' is tolerated).

entries.snippet:
const params = new URLSearchParams()
params.set("q", "hello world")
params.set("page", "2")
console.log(params.toString())  // q=hello%20world&page=2
differences: **Single value per key**: a repeated query-string key (`?a=1&a=2`) silently keeps only its last value — `.get()`/`.getAll()` never see the first one, so `.getAll()` never returns more than one element
There is no true multi-value `.append()`, since it can't be represented faithfully on top of the `Map<string,string>` backing structure

entries.name: URLPattern
entries.signature: new URLPattern(init?: { protocol?; hostname?; port?; pathname?; search?; hash? }): URLPattern
entries.description: WHATWG route matching. Each component pattern compiles once at construction to an anchored PCRE2 regex; .test/.exec match a full URL string, which parses via libcurl's URL API. An omitted init component defaults to "*" and reads back as such from the component fields. An unparseable input is false/null, never a throw; an invalid pattern throws a catchable TypeError at construction.
differences: Object-literal init only, over `protocol`/`hostname`/`port`/`pathname`/`search`/`hash` — no constructor-string form, no `baseURL`, no `username`/`password` components
Pattern grammar is literals, `\` escapes, `*`, `:name`, and `:name?` — `{}` groups, `+` modifiers, and inline `(regex)` groups throw a `TypeError` at construction

`.exec()` returns a merged `Map<string, string> | null` of every named group across components (an unset optional group is absent), not the spec's per-component `URLPatternResult` object — needs the deferred dynamic object model
`*` wildcards aren't exposed as numbered groups; no `hasRegExpGroups`
